summary: Extend the approved Clinical Glass / Continuity Aurora system into one finished SaaS product experience: a memorable three-card arrival under ‘Built around everyone responsible for tomorrow.’, selective supporting reveals, a buyer-oriented four-part business model, cheaper scroll surfaces, and coherent patient, staff, caregiver, system, sign-in, modal, and shared-chrome presentation without changing the deterministic workflow or caregiver boundary.
existing_design_system: docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md and the approved LAND-001 frontend design/report evidence

visual_direction.layout: Preserve LAND-001's public-page order, hero, Continuity Field, readiness proof, Louisiana map, FAQ, closing CTA, anchors, and workspace destinations. The role-card section remains the signature midpoint. Replace the current three deployment-tier cards with a four-part SaaS operating-model sequence: (1) ‘Institutional buyer’ — cancer centers, oncology service lines, and health systems responsible for pre-treatment operations; (2) ‘Subscribed capability’ — one treatment-readiness workspace spanning patient check-in, accountable exception routing, the readiness graph, and permission-limited logistics; (3) ‘Configured implementation’ — align sites, roles, routing rules, escalation windows, and readiness checkpoints to the organization’s operating model; and (4) ‘Expansion path’ — extend the same capability across additional sites, treatment programs, and operating roles. Use the section label ‘SaaS business model’, a heading such as ‘One readiness capability, shaped around the oncology operation.’, and the existing workspace-entry action labeled ‘Explore the product workspaces’; do not add pricing, checkout, a fake sales flow, customer proof, or disclaimer panels. Across the application, retain generous editorial spacing only on public/patient surfaces; sign-in uses a clear role-entry grid; staff keeps a compact desktop rail and dense content canvas; caregiver remains a narrow logistics view; system retains graph, timeline, and architecture order. Remove the staff content area's independent vertical scroller so the document is the expected primary scroll container; bounded modal bodies and wide tables may keep local overflow.
visual_direction.color: Keep the established cool-white/cream canvas, ink text, indigo action, mint resolution, amber risk, and landing-only coral/lavender atmosphere. Replace the older peach sticker fills, hard two-pixel ink outlines, and candy shadows with three Clinical Glass tiers: canvas; quiet translucent/near-opaque panels with one-pixel cool borders; and raised action/status panels with a compact soft shadow. Use translucency without blur on repeated scrolling cards. Reserve blur, if production profiling supports it, for small isolated chrome only; the landing header, footer, full staff rail, large modal overlay, and broad card fields use near-opaque fills instead of scroll-attached backdrop filters. Patient surfaces may use warmer indigo/mint light, caregiver uses mint-tinted privacy/logistics emphasis, staff uses mostly white/slate with semantic accents, and system uses ink/indigo structure. Coral and lavender never encode clinical state, and every risk/ready state retains an icon plus text label.
visual_direction.typography: Retain Outfit for display and Poppins/Plus Jakarta Sans for body, with JetBrains Mono limited to identifiers and timestamps. Keep the landing's expressive type scale, but use a calmer 28–36px patient/sign-in hierarchy and compact 18–28px staff/system headings. Replace shouty or excessive uppercase where it slows reading; short eyebrow and status labels may remain uppercase. Preserve tabular numerals and dense metadata in staff views. Public copy speaks as a finished buyer-facing SaaS product: remove landing-visible ‘demo’, ‘prototype’, ‘preview’, ‘portfolio’, and ‘training environment’ framing; replace ‘FHIR R4 mapping preview’ with standards-shaped workflow language; replace the FAQ's caveat-style ‘what the current product represents’ wording with operational-fit language; and replace the closing training-workspace sentence with an invitation to follow the readiness workflow. Keep required synthetic/simulated or not-connected labels at the specific in-product record, map, transport, or mapping boundary where they are meaningful, not as a global product identity or public disclaimer theme.
visual_direction.spacing_and_shape: Use the existing 4/8px rhythm and 10/16/24 radii. Public cards retain 24–32px editorial radii; patient, caregiver, sign-in, system, and modal panels use 16–24px; dense staff rows, inputs, tabs, and metric tiles use 10–16px. Convert hard 2px outlines to 1px structural borders except where a control needs a deliberate high-contrast boundary. Maintain at least 44px public/patient targets and comfortable mobile field spacing; staff desktop controls may be compact while staying keyboard usable. Give images, maps, canvas, graph panels, and asynchronous/fallback content explicit dimensions or aspect ratios so no entrance or load state shifts surrounding layout.
visual_direction.component_presentation: Create a shared presentation vocabulary rather than per-page restyling: Clinical Panel (quiet and raised), semantic Status Chip, compact Metric Tile, segmented Filter Rail, indigo Primary and bordered Secondary buttons, glass Input, and icon wells using the existing tokens. Public header/footer and official logo remain recognizable, with the navigation label changed from ‘Deployment’ to ‘Business model’. The landing product proof reads as a polished sample readiness record rather than a training frame. Workspace gateway and auth modal become a truthful local role selector (‘Workspace gateway’ / ‘Choose a role-based workspace’) rather than claiming real authentication or enterprise access controls. Patient home keeps the dark appointment anchor and one-clear-action readiness banner, restyled as refined Clinical Glass; readiness and confirmation modals share the same header, fields, validation summary, disabled, loading, and success language. Staff rail, Command Center, Exceptions, Patients, case tabs, Resources, Insights, Integrations, and Admin reuse compact panels, one-pixel dividers, small shadows, and semantic status markers while retaining all owners, due cues, data, and controls. Caregiver shows only appointment and transport projection plus the explicit privacy boundary; no clinical text or nurse details enter its DOM. System graph nodes, event timeline, inspector, and architecture cards adopt the same surfaces and preserve icons/text as state cues. Shared header, dropdown, footer, dock, buttons, fields, map frame, modal surfaces, selected tabs, and focus rings all use this vocabulary. The existing official identity, state callbacks, routes, reducer, persistence, task actions, audit events, and map fallback remain authoritative.

motion.strategy: Use one small progressive-enhancement reveal primitive backed by a shared IntersectionObserver, CSS variables/data attributes, and visible-by-default markup. The role-card group observes at approximately 0.18 intersection with a modest negative bottom root margin, reveals once, and unobserves completed targets. Patient uses ‘guided lift’ (opacity 0 to 1, translate3d(-18px, 22px, 0) to rest, 540ms); staff uses ‘center resolve’ (opacity 0 to 1, translate3d(0, 28px, 0) plus scale 0.975 to rest, 620ms); caregiver uses ‘supported arrival’ (opacity 0 to 1, translate3d(18px, 22px, 0) to rest, 560ms). Start delays are 0/80/160ms in patient-staff-caregiver order and all use cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). On narrow screens keep the family distinct but reduce horizontal travel to -8/0/+8px and vertical travel to 18–24px. Transforms do not affect layout; cards are interactive throughout; a focused unrevealed target is immediately promoted to its final state; temporary will-change is removed after arrival. If JavaScript, IntersectionObserver, or enhancement setup fails, no pre-reveal class is applied and content stays visible. No raw scroll listener, reveal requestAnimationFrame loop, repeated layout read, scroll-jacking, pinned section, or parallax is introduced.
motion.transitions: Keep hover/press/focus feedback at 140–200ms and state-panel changes at 180–240ms. The signature role arrivals use the exact 540/620/560ms variants above. Use only two supporting entrances: workflow-step cards rise 14px and fade over 440ms with 60ms group staggering, while the four SaaS-model cards rise 12px and sharpen from scale 0.99 over 460ms with 55ms staggering. Their headings remain immediately visible and each group runs once. Do not entrance-animate hero content, proof metrics, the live graph, map, FAQ rows, operational workspace cards, urgent statuses, or every section. Existing graph dash/pulse, route scrolling, dock movement, FAQ chevron, modal entrance, and confirmation celebration must all follow effective reduced motion. Animate only opacity and transform for entrances; color, border, and shadow transitions remain small and do not become persistent composited layers.
motion.microinteractions: Role cards keep the existing subtle image scale and arrow nudge on hover, with a smaller 2px lift and no hover transform for touch or reduced motion. Buttons use a 1–2px lift on hover, settle on press, and never use the older offset-block bounce shadow. Selected tabs/nav items use fill plus a text/icon state, filters retain clear pressed selection, form validation moves focus to the summary/first invalid field without shaking, and successful task/plan changes use mint icon-plus-copy emphasis. FAQ expansion is an immediate semantic show/hide with only the chevron rotation when motion is allowed. Modals use a short opacity/12px entrance, then manage focus without animation delays. The map's static fallback occupies the final frame while the live Leaflet module is loaded near the viewport; failure simply retains the labeled fallback. Confirmation confetti is allowed only when neither the system nor product control requests reduced motion.
motion.reduced_motion: Effective reduced motion is the union of live prefers-reduced-motion and the existing in-product motion-off control. Under either signal, the reveal primitive never applies a hidden/transformed pending state, observer work is skipped or immediately completed, smooth anchor scrolling becomes auto, role/workflow/SaaS cards render in their final positions, modal and FAQ changes are immediate, graph dash/pulse and all animate-pop/fade/slide utilities stop, dock and hover transforms stop, the Continuity Field renders its current static resting form, and confetti is suppressed. Content order, labels, focus movement, validation, selected/disabled/loading/success states, route changes, task transitions, and plan confirmation remain identical. The global CSS path must support both the media query and the .motion-reduce class so user-selected motion off is as complete as the operating-system preference.

responsive.strategy: Remain mobile-first from 320px. Role, workflow, and SaaS groups are one column on mobile; role reveal travel is reduced and never causes page overflow. At 768px, use two-column workspace/sign-in modules and a two-by-two SaaS model; at 1024px+, use the approved landing splits, three role cards, four connected SaaS cards, and the dense staff rail. The staff mobile navigation remains an in-flow wrapped compact grid with 44px targets rather than a competing vertical scroller; desktop staff navigation may be sticky below shared chrome while document scrolling owns page movement. Patient/caregiver/system content stays one column until space genuinely supports paired panels. Graph nodes stack in reading/dependency order on narrow screens, tab/filter rails may scroll horizontally inside their own labeled control only, tables/preformatted mappings may use bounded horizontal overflow, and no component creates horizontal page overflow.
responsive.notes: Verify 320px, 390x844, 768px, 1440x900, and a wide desktop. Preserve safe-area padding for the mobile dock and enough bottom padding that it never covers the last focusable control. Keep the header, role images, Continuity Field, maps, avatars, and graph nodes dimensioned to prevent layout shift. Modals are bottom-sheet-like at mobile sizes and centered panels above 640px, with a single bounded internal scroll area, sticky actions that do not cover focused inputs, Escape/close behavior, initial focus, focus containment, and trigger-focus restoration. The landing map defers live-map import/mount until near the viewport and shows the existing static fallback immediately; below-fold imagery uses explicit dimensions plus lazy decoding/loading. Remove body background-attachment: fixed, broad header/footer/rail/card backdrop-filter, and the staff inner overflow-y-auto; retain the Continuity Field's DPR cap, offscreen/hidden pause, idle settling, and fallback unchanged.

application_states: Landing default: finished-product SaaS posture, approved hero/Continuity Aurora composition, buyer-value copy, and no demo/prototype/preview/portfolio/training framing.
Landing progressive enhancement unavailable: all headings, role cards, workflow cards, SaaS cards, actions, and links are visible and usable without an observer or animation support.
Signature role-card pending/revealed: patient guided lift, staff center resolve, caregiver supported arrival; each reveals once and ends in the same stable card layout.
SaaS business model: institutional buyer, subscribed capability, configured implementation, and expansion path, with one existing workspace-entry CTA and no price/checkout state.
Map loading/error/offline: a dimensionally stable, labeled static corridor is the immediate and permanent fallback; the live map upgrades in place only when available near the viewport.

Workspace gateway/auth selector: default role cards, keyboard focus/pressed feedback, modal open/close, and the same patient/staff/caregiver/system destinations without claiming production authentication.
Patient readiness default: screening pending, one primary readiness action, treatment details, and stable supporting cards.
Readiness modal validation/loading/success: visible error summary and field association, disabled routing action with in-progress label, and route completion without losing focus context.

Patient workflow progression: triage in progress, updated plan ready, acknowledgment disabled until agreement, confirming, and confirmed success; reduced motion suppresses confetti but preserves the success state.

Staff Command Center/Exceptions/Patients/case/Resources/Insights/Integrations/Admin: compact default, hover/focus/selected, actionable versus disabled records, filtered/no-result directory with clear-filter recovery, pending versus completed tasks, and graph/tab selection.
Caregiver logistics pending/confirmed/map-visible: explicit privacy boundary and only appointment/transport data in every state.

System graph/timeline: unscreened, active blocker, acknowledged/in progress, staff-resolved awaiting patient, plan confirmed, node selected/closed, role filter selected, and empty filtered timeline if applicable.
Global motion modes: normal, live OS reduced motion, and user motion off all preserve content, route, focus, and workflow equivalence.
Responsive/shared chrome: landing and workspace header, dropdown, footer, staff rail/mobile tools, and mobile dock remain reachable without clipping, page overflow, or covered focus targets.
Reset and persistence: current visual state reflects restored workflow data; reset returns the known landing/opening state without changing domain behavior.
accessibility: Preserve semantic landmarks and heading order; implement role/workspace entry cards as native buttons where practical rather than div role=button replicas.

Keep the existing high-contrast 2px indigo focus outline plus offset on every interactive element; entrance opacity/transform never removes content from the accessibility tree, and focus immediately completes a pending reveal.
Maintain WCAG AA text/control contrast, 44px minimum public/patient/mobile targets, keyboard-operable navigation, filters, FAQ, graph nodes, forms, and map fallback links/labels.
Every ready/risk/pending/selected/disabled/success state combines icon, text, shape or border treatment with color; motion and color are never the sole status carrier.
Both reduced-motion sources render final content immediately and disable reveal, smooth scroll, pulses/dashes, confetti, dock transforms, modal movement, and decorative hover movement.

Modal open moves focus into the dialog, Escape and an explicit close control work, focus is contained while open, and closing restores the invoking control; validation is announced and associated with invalid fields.

Caregiver rendering continues to derive only from deriveCaregiverProjection; clinical concern text, nurse notes, diagnosis-only detail, and nurse-only action data stay absent from visible content and the DOM/accessible name tree.

Maintain intrinsic sizes/aspect ratios for official logos, images, canvas, maps, and graph panels to avoid cumulative layout shift; meaningful images retain useful alt text and decorative imagery remains empty-alt/aria-hidden.

Automated checks should mock IntersectionObserver to prove distinct variants, one-time unobserve, focus-to-reveal, no-observer fallback, and both reduced-motion paths; copy tests should reject demo/prototype/preview/portfolio/training terms in the rendered landing surface.

Production-browser checks should confirm document scrolling and Page Up/Page Down/touch/wheel behavior, scrollWidth no greater than clientWidth at target viewports, no focus target hidden under sticky/fixed chrome, and no reveal-caused long task of 50ms or more during the measured full-page pass.
assets_or_dependencies: Reuse the official oncoready-title-logo.svg and compact continuity-loop mark; do not redraw or recolor the identity.
Reuse the existing story imagery with explicit dimensions, lazy loading, and async decoding below the fold.

Reuse React, TypeScript, Tailwind/CSS, Lucide/Tabler icons, the existing motion package where already present, native IntersectionObserver, Leaflet/static RideMap fallback, and the current ContinuityField canvas.
Add no new animation, scrolling, styling, data, backend, analytics, or infrastructure dependency.
design_system_changes: Extend Clinical Glass with quiet and raised no-blur panel tiers so repeated workspace cards can share the landing's visual language without broad backdrop-filter cost.
Add a named one-time arrival family: guided lift, center resolve, and supported arrival, plus the exact duration/easing/stagger/reduced-motion behavior in this report.

Add performance rules: no fixed body background, no broad scroll-attached blur, document-owned workspace scrolling, lazy near-viewport live maps, temporary will-change only, and no reveal scroll listener or render loop.
Add workspace density guidance: editorial public/patient rhythm, compact staff geometry, mint logistics/privacy emphasis for caregiver, and structural ink/indigo hierarchy for system views.

Add product-presentation guidance: buyer-oriented SaaS language on public surfaces; scoped illustrative/simulated/not-connected labeling only where a specific workflow record or boundary requires it; no global training/demo identity.

No design-system documentation file changes are made in Phase A; this approved report defines the extension to implement and can be incorporated into docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md during Phase B without changing the approved direction.
notes_for_codex: Phase A inspected every current perspective, all eight staff destinations, shared chrome/modals, existing tests, and the known fixed-background, broad-blur, map, canvas, and nested-scroll candidates. No backend, database, contract, architecture, route, workflow-state, persistence, audit, or caregiver-projection change is needed.
The signature role-card variants and supporting workflow/SaaS variants above are the approved motion specification; do not generalize entrance animation to every landing or workspace card.
Implementation should first remove the fixed body background and broad blur/nested staff scroll costs, then add progressive reveal so performance is improved before motion is layered on.

Use a near-viewport gate for the live Leaflet upgrade and preserve the current static map fallback. Preserve ContinuityField's existing DPR cap, offscreen/hidden pause, idle settling, live OS preference response, product motion-off input, and canvas-unavailable fallback.

The public copy audit includes trust signals, readiness proof chrome, business-model navigation/section, FAQ framing, closing CTA, and shared landing footer. Product-internal synthetic/simulated mapping and transport boundaries remain truthful without branding the product as a training environment.

Phase B verification should include build and existing smoke tests; focused reveal/fallback/reduced-motion/copy tests; browser checks at 320, 390x844, 768, 1440x900, and wide desktop; route reachability for all staff destinations; search/filter/no-result states; FAQ and map fallback; the complete Maria journey; caregiver DOM exclusion; reset/persistence; and a production-mode scroll trace.
Ready for orchestrator compatibility review and exact canonical design-report digest binding. Any change to this report after approval requires a new review before production frontend edits.
